note: lxpt relay core v1 (spec/floor-v1.md section 5). Generated by python/gen_core_fixtures.py from the Python reference; every value is a TEST value and every signature a filler (the host verifies before the core sees a CLAIM or RELEASE). Each scenario builds one Relay (relay_hash, limits, talk_limit_s) and runs its steps in order: 'do' is admit, client, peer, tick, leg_down, peer_up, peer_rtt or peer_down; 'at' is the clock in ms; 'hex' the bytes received; 'rx' when they were received if not 'at'. 'expect' is every line the step produced, in order: 'admit ok|no' for an admit, 'send c<leg>|p<peer> <hex>' and 'note <channel tag> <floor action>'. Scenarios named sim_R<n> are traces recorded at relay n of python/sim.py's fixture run. A 'ticks' step is a run of 'count' ticks 'every' ms apart from 'at', none of which produced a line.

scenarios.name: one_relay_spurt
scenarios.note: SUBs, a CLAIM forwarded, granted, frames to voice legs only, a duplicate dropped, HEARD upstream, RELEASE forwarded, heartbeats

scenarios.name: narrow_leg_profile
scenarios.note: a BLE leg makes the spurt Codec2 and gets its frames; an Opus spurt skips it

scenarios.name: admission_rate_limit
scenarios.note: two new claims per channel per second; retries pass; stale ones are dropped

scenarios.name: emergency_rate_limit
scenarios.note: one Emergency claim per identity per channel per 10 s

scenarios.name: busy_yield_carry_the_claim
scenarios.note: BUSY and YIELD are preceded by the holder's CLAIM

scenarios.name: peers
scenarios.note: peer up, PEER summaries with split horizon, a remote claim and its TALKING, frames both ways, TALKING forwarded at most once a second, peer lost after 15 s

scenarios.name: late_joiners
scenarios.note: a leg or a peer that newly lists a channel with a live spurt gets its CLAIM and TALKING

scenarios.name: leases
scenarios.note: a SUB lease runs 60 s; a released leg goes at once; an empty channel is freed

scenarios.name: stale_frames_count_as_heard
scenarios.note: a frame older than 500 ms is not forwarded but still counts as heard

scenarios.name: settle_from_peer_rtt
scenarios.note: the settle window is the largest RTT of peers on the channel, capped at 300 ms

scenarios.name: garbage_and_misdirected
scenarios.note: undecodable bytes and messages on the wrong side are ignored

scenarios.name: small_tables
scenarios.note: channels, spurts and dedup at their limits
